 You’ve tried the viral Korean skincare, mastered (or attempted) the K-pop choreography and probably have a few K-beauty staples on your shelf. Now, it’s time to give your scalp and strands their own K-beauty moment By Ruman Baig November 3, 2026 Jun Ji-hyun attends the Saint Laurent Womenswear Spring/Summer 2027 show. Photo: Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images If I had a dirham for every time I’ve had a skincare issue and someone recommended Korean skincare, I’d be a millionaire by now. Haircare, on the other hand? I’d have exactly one dirham, and that’s because I’d be the one recommending Korean haircare to everyone else. We’ve spent so long obsessing over the skin on our faces that we’ve collectively forgotten we have skin on our heads, too. When it comes to skincare, Korean beauty has long set the gold standard. But here’s the thing: Korea has been working the same magic on haircare, too. The rest of the world just hasn’t caught on yet. Consider this your introduction to the world of K-haircare. Let’s get into it.
 The secret is… in the scalp Before we get into the brands worth adding to your haircare shelf, let’s talk about what sets K-haircare apart. Think of it as skincare’s approach to hair, with the scalp taking centre stage. Rather than focusing solely on the lengths and ends, many Korean haircare routines start at the roots, with targeted formulas designed to cleanse the scalp, manage excess oil, soothe dryness and care for damaged strands. The multi-step approach will feel familiar to any K-beauty enthusiast, with scalp scrubs, exfoliating treatments, tonics and nourishing masks sitting alongside your everyday shampoo and conditioner. Ingredients are another part of the appeal, with ginseng, camellia oil and fermented extracts drawing on traditional Korean beauty practices and modern formulation techniques. The idea is simple – give your scalp the care it needs, while treating the hair itself with formulas tailored to its specific concerns. And much like skincare, it’s less about following every step and more about finding what works for you.
 Double cleanse, double the difference? Cleansing is probably the most overlooked step in haircare. Think about it, those quick showers before work, the post-workout rinse squeezed in between meetings and the perpetual feeling that you’re on a timer. But how often do we actually stop to think about whether we’re washing our hair properly? In Korean haircare, cleansing is less about getting in and getting out, and more about creating the right foundation for everything that follows. That can mean paying closer attention to the scalp, using a targeted scalp cleanser when needed and following up with a shampoo that removes excess oil, sweat and product buildup without stripping the scalp. Some routines also incorporate scalp exfoliators or tonics, depending on individual needs. Because here's the thing: you can invest in the most expensive masks, serums and leave-in treatments on the market, but if your scalp isn't clean and well cared for, you're not giving your hair the best possible starting point. Double cleansing isn't necessarily a must for everyone, but a more thoughtful approach to washing? That's a good place to start.
 Your shampoo and conditioner need backup What if I told you that no matter how good your shampoo and conditioner are, they’re not equipped to fight all your hair battles? Think of it this way, using only moisturiser and sunscreen in your skincare routine will get the basics covered, but if you’re after that glazed-doughnut glow, you’ll probably want to bring in a few more targeted products. The same logic applies to your haircare. Scalp treatments, exfoliators, serums and tonics all have a role to play, but knowing when to reach for what is what makes the difference.
 A scalp exfoliator, for instance, can help lift dead skin cells and product buildup, making it a useful addition if your scalp feels congested. Serums and tonics can offer targeted care for concerns such as dryness or excess oil, while a soothing formula may help calm an irritated scalp. Regular scalp massages are another feature of many Korean haircare routines, helping distribute products and temporarily increasing blood flow to the area, although evidence that massage alone promotes hair growth remains limited. If dandruff is the concern, a treatment formulated with proven anti-dandruff ingredients is a better bet than relying on a scrub alone.
 The trick is to stop treating haircare as a one-size-fits-all situation and start building a routine around your hair’s texture, density, condition and your scalp’s needs. Oily roots, a dry or flaky scalp, fine strands that fall flat and lengths that have seen one too many heat-styling sessions all call for different approaches. Consider it a calculated regime, not a 12-step routine for the sake of it. Because before you start adding everything to your cart, you need to know what you’re trying to fix, which product can help and how often you actually need it.
 Once you’ve figured out what your hair actually needs, it’s time for the fun part, adding to cart. And because we wouldn’t leave you to navigate the world of K-haircare alone, we’ve rounded up the tried-and-tested Korean haircare heroes worth investing in. Your scalp (and your shopping cart) can thank us later.
